title: Small object down a drain
prompt: Output: one WAV, 48 kHz / 16-bit / stereo, exactly 144,000 samples (3.0 s at 30 fps = 90 frames). Python + numpy/scipy only. Synthesise everything (no samples, no downloads, no speech). Fixed random seed (np.random.default_rng(55)). A 3-second foley moment: a small chalk stick dropping into a street drain. Frame 0: a light dry tap on wet stone (3 ms noise burst, bandpass 2.5 kHz, plus a short 1.1 kHz resonant tick). Frames 6-24: two smaller bounces, each 40% quieter and closer together. Frame 24: it falls in: a hollow metallic clink against a grate (inharmonic modal partials at 1, 2.32, 4.25, 6.63 x 870 Hz, 250 ms decay), then frames 30-60 a fall echo inside a pipe (comb filter at 7 ms + 21 ms feedback, low-passed), ending in a tiny distant plop at frame 66 (a sine 'bubble' sweeping 400→1100 Hz in 40 ms). Under everything, quiet rain bed (filtered pink noise, -24 dB relative) fading out by frame 90. Mono-centred source, rain wide. Master: -14 LUFS integrated, true peak <= -1 dBTP (4x oversampled peak check), last frames fade to exactly 0. You can't listen, so verify: measure loudness and true peak with ffmpeg ebur128 (peak=true), check the exact sample count, confirm the energy change lands on each cue frame, check every note fits the chord under it, render a spectrogram PNG and inspect it. Fix and re-render until every check passes, then report the numbers.
notes: Foley: dry tap, two quieter bounces, grate clink into a darkening pipe echo, tiny bubble plop at frame 66 over quiet rain.
